title: Town Talk (1903-10-02)

The Public School concert was a great success last Friday. There was a large attendance, and everything passed off without a hitch. For travelling on the railway without tickets two men were fined £2 each last Saturday at the local police court. A truck of motor cars arrived at Katoomba last Saturday consigned to Mr. Mark Foy, Medlow. It is said he intends running them to the various sights this summer. Mr. J. Waudby, baker, &c., is now to be found in his new shop, opposite the railway station. title: News in Brief (1905-09-01)
context: Mountaineer (Katoomba, NSW : 1894 - 1908), Friday 1 September 1905, page 6 News in Brief. — There were no cases at the Katoomba police court during the past week. — Snow fell on the Mountains on Tuesday night last, the ground being covered on Wednesday morning. The Mountains around looked very picturesque in their garb of dazzling white. — The tourist association has received word from the railway commissioners that they cannot run a daily tourist train to the Mountains as requested by the Association. context: n Hartley this election, but no names are mentioned yet. It will be a "dead bird" for John if more than one candidate opposes him. Preparations are being made at Blackheath for active work at the rifle range. The membership of the club has increased by nearly a dozen lately. Mr. Harry Levien, looking sleek and well, but very much whiter than when we last saw him, was in attendance at the Katoomba Police Court on Wednesday last. He won his case in about seven minutes, and pocketed a big fee, as usual. If Lithgow obtains the iron contract - and it seems more than probable - it will be a good thing for Katoomba.
